lines: A granular tape recorder: audio is recorded onto a reel, the reel is cut into segments by markers, and grains are played back from the current segment under knob and CV control
Crossfades the output between the incoming audio fully left and reel playback fully right; while recording over existing audio in replace mode it also sets how much of the old recording is kept
Sets the length of the grain read from the current segment: the whole segment fully left, about 1ms fully right, on a fourth-power curve
Scales the voltage at the grain size CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the GRAIN knob
Sets playback speed and direction: stopped at centre, forward to twice speed fully right, backwards at about 4.5 times speed fully left, though the manual calls that end 26 semitones down
Scales the voltage at the speed CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the SPEED knob
Sets how much the grains overlap: gaps between them below 15%, one seamless grain to 35%, two voices to 50%, three with stereo panning to 70%, and four with random pitch above that
Offsets where in the current segment the grain is read from: the start of the segment fully left, as far in as the grain length allows fully right
Scales the voltage at the scan CV input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the SCAN knob
Steps through the markers on the reel and moves playback to the one chosen; its top value follows the number of markers and it reads out from 1
Pressing it starts recording the input onto the reel and pressing it again stops; with a cable in the clock input recording begins on the next clock edge instead of immediately
Pressing it drops a marker at the playback position, cutting another segment out of the reel
Pressing it moves playback to the next marker, wrapping round after the last one
Pressing it deletes every marker, sets the marker count back to four and returns SLCT to its first position
Pressing it spreads markers evenly across the reel, stepping through 4, 8 and 16 on successive presses
Sets what pressing REC does to audio already on the reel: replace wipes the reel and every marker first, overdub keeps them and adds the new audio from the playback position
The left audio input, recorded onto the reel and crossfaded to the output by MIX, with ±5V taken as full scale
The right audio input; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both channels
Shifts the MIX crossfade, 8V covering the whole of the knob's travel; the total of knob and voltage is held inside that travel
Shifts the grain length after scaling by its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole of the GRAIN knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the playback speed after scaling by its attenuverter, 4V covering the whole of the SPEED knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the grain overlap, 5V covering the whole of the DENS knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the scan offset after scaling by its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole of the SCAN knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the marker chosen by SLCT, 5V covering the whole run of markers; the total is held inside that run
A rising edge past 2.5V starts the next grain when DENS is below about half, or sets the grain length to the measured clock period above it
Playback runs while this is above 2.5V and stops at the end of the grain once it falls; with nothing patched it counts as held high
A rising edge past 2.5V starts recording, and the next one stops it
A rising edge past 2.5V drops a marker at the playback position
A rising edge past 2.5V moves playback to the next marker
A rising edge past 2.5V deletes every marker and returns SLCT to its first position
A rising edge past 2.5V spreads markers evenly across the reel, stepping through 4, 8 and 16 on successive edges
The left output: the incoming audio and the reel playback mixed by MIX at ±5V, or the expander's processed signal when one is fitted
The right output: the incoming audio and the reel playback mixed by MIX at ±5V, or the expander's processed signal when one is fitted
An envelope follower on the output, 0V in silence and rising to 8V at full level
A 10V pulse 1ms long at the end of every grain and every segment
Note — the reel is empty when the module is added, so nothing plays until you record onto it with REC or load a WAV file from the panel menu
Note — the SPEED knob comes up at its centre, where playback is stopped, so a freshly added module is silent until it is moved off centre
Note — clicking the waveform display drops a marker at that point, clicking an existing marker moves playback to it, and right-clicking a marker deletes it
Note — a Tapestry Expander placed immediately to the right takes over the two audio outputs, feeding them through its bit crusher and filter
Note — two buttons held together give extra actions: REC with NXT levels the incoming audio, and REC with MRK records into a new segment
Note — NXT held with MRK deletes the current marker, and NXT held with REC deletes the audio of the current segment
Note — holding NXT with MRK for 3 seconds deletes every marker, and holding NXT with REC for 3 seconds erases the whole reel
Menu — Load Reel... — opens a file dialog and reads a WAV file onto the reel
Menu — Save Reel... — writes the reel out as a WAV file
Menu — Clear Reel — erases the recorded audio
Menu — Splice Count: 4 (click to cycle) — spreads that many markers evenly across the reel and steps the count on through 4, 8 and 16
Menu — Waveform Color: Red, Amber, Green, Baby Blue, Peach, Pink, White — sets the colour the recorded waveform is drawn in

Tapestry.notes: SPEED is asymmetric in a way the maker's own comment and QUICKSTART.md contradict: dsp/tapestry-core.h:383-398 raises 2 to the power of semitones/12 for both directions, so the reverse end of the knob plays backwards at about 4.5 times speed rather than the 26 semitones down that kVariSpeedDownSemitones and the manual describe. QUICKSTART.md also says centre is normal forward playback; the code has a dead zone of 0.02 either side of centre that stops playback outright (dsp/tapestry-core.h:368-377), and the knob's default is centre, so a freshly added module is silent. The panel menu still uses the maker's older wording, Splice and Reel, where the panel prints MRK.

lines: An effects expander for Tapestry, adding a bit crusher and a 24dB per octave resonant lowpass filter to its output; it goes immediately to the right of Tapestry
Sets the bit depth the crusher rounds the signal to: 16 bits fully right, 1 bit fully left
Sets how many samples the crusher holds each value for: one fully left, 64 fully right
Crossfades between Tapestry's audio and the bit-crushed version of it, with the crusher out of circuit fully left
Sets the filter cutoff on a logarithmic scale, 20Hz fully left to 20kHz fully right, and never above 45% of the sample rate
Sets the filter resonance, none fully left up to a feedback factor of nearly 4 fully right, trimmed back slightly as the cutoff rises
Crossfades between the bit crusher's output and the filtered version of it, with the filter out of circuit fully left
Sets the gain applied after both effects: silence fully left, unity at centre, twice fully right, after which the signal is soft-clipped and held inside ±1.5
Shifts the bit depth, 1V for one and a half bits; the total of knob and voltage is held between 1 and 16 bits
Shifts the sample hold length, 10V covering the whole of the RATE knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the bit crusher's dry-wet balance, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the filter cutoff, 1V moving it by about an octave; the total of knob and voltage is held inside the knob's travel
Shifts the filter resonance, 10V covering the whole of the RES knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the filter's dry-wet balance, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Note — with no Tapestry immediately to its left this module does nothing at all: it reads no audio, writes no audio and returns before any knob is read, and its green lamp stays dark
Note — the processed audio is handed back to Tapestry and leaves through Tapestry's own output jacks, which is why this module has no output of its own
Note — both dry-wet knobs come up fully left, so a freshly placed expander passes Tapestry's audio through with only a 20Hz DC blocker and the output gain applied

TapestryExpander.notes: The filter's cutoff CV works out at almost exactly 1V per octave by coincidence rather than by design: TapestryExpander.cpp:160 adds a tenth of the voltage to a knob that dsp/tapestry-effects.h:88-92 maps logarithmically from 20Hz to 20kHz, and a thousandfold range over a tenth of the travel is a factor of 1.995. It is not declared as tracking and it shifts with the sample rate, since the top of the range is held to 45% of it.

lines: A fuzz and phase-locked-loop harmoniser: the input is squared into a fuzz, a tracking oscillator follows its pitch at a chosen interval, and a divider adds a subharmonic, the three then mixed together
Sets the level of the squared fuzz voice in the mix, on an audio taper
Sets the level of the subharmonic voice in the mix, on an audio taper
Sets the level of the tracking oscillator's voice in the mix, on an audio taper
Sets the gain applied to the mix, 0.02 fully left rising to 1.74 fully right, after which the output is clipped
Chooses the subharmonic interval by dividing its clock by 2 to 9: an octave down at the first position, three octaves and a major second down at the last
Chooses what clocks the subharmonic divider: the squared input, or the tracking oscillator
Chooses what the loop's control voltage does: glide, where it slews towards the tracked pitch, or vibrato, where a triangle is added to it as well
Sets the speed of the frequency modulator, about 0.45Hz to 95Hz of glide or 0.55Hz to 18.5Hz of vibrato, and with it how hard the loop is pumped towards the tracked pitch
Chooses the oscillator's interval by multiplying the tracked pitch by 1 to 8: unison at the first position, three octaves up at the last
Divides the input's edges by one, two or four before the loop compares them, so the oscillator tracks an octave or two octaves lower
The signal the module processes, with ±5V taken as full scale, despite the panel printing CV IN
Shifts the level of the squared voice, 10V covering the whole of the SQR MIX knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the level of the subharmonic voice, 10V covering the whole of the SUB MIX knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the level of the oscillator voice, 10V covering the whole of the OSC MIX knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the frequency modulator's speed, 10V covering the whole of the RATE knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Steps the subharmonic interval, 10V covering all eight positions of the SUB PGM knob; the total is rounded to a position and held inside them
Steps the oscillator's interval, 10V covering all eight positions of the OSC PGM knob; the total is rounded to a position and held inside them
The three voices mixed and scaled by VOLUME, ±5V at full scale and never beyond ±6.75V, despite the panel printing CV OUT
The squared fuzz voice on its own at ±5V, taken before the mix knobs
The subharmonic voice on its own at ±5V, taken before the mix knobs
The tracking oscillator's voice on its own at ±5V, taken before the mix knobs
How firmly the loop is locked, 0V when it is not tracking and rising to 10V when the oscillator reaches the multiple of the input pitch set by OSC PGM
Note — every voice is scaled by an envelope follower on the input, so all of them fall silent when the input does and the module makes no sound of its own
Note — three lamps report the loop: green that the input is loud enough to track, blue how firm the lock is, red how far the loop is from it
Note — the pitch is taken from the rising edges of the heavily squared input, so the module follows one note at a time
Note — the number of channels at the audio input sets the channel count of every output, with a separate loop and divider run for each channel

Korupt.notes: The panel letters the main audio jacks CV IN and CV OUT, while the maker's own tooltips call both of them Audio and Korupt.cpp:151 writes an audio mix there; the lines follow the code and name the conflict. The lock output is a continuous confidence figure rather than a gate (korupt-dsp.h:404-415), so it is coloured cv. The oscillator's own range is 18Hz to the lesser of 9800Hz and 36% of the sample rate (korupt-dsp.h:353-358), which caps how high the chosen interval can actually reach.

lines: A self-contained voice and external processor: a tone core, a feedback delay and filter network, an internal gesture generator and an ambient reverb, with six momentary pads for playing the feedback
Sets the gain and saturation applied to the external input before its CV is taken, clean fully left and heavily driven fully right
Sets how much of the processed external signal is injected into the tone core
Sets the standing activation of the tone core, which is what makes it sound with nothing patched
Sets how much of the delay and filter feedback is mixed into the activation, and how much of it bleeds through when activation is low
Scales the voltage at the ACT CV jack, -1 to +1, before it is added to the activation
Sets the pitch of the tone core, 20Hz fully left to 10kHz fully right, although the readout claims 500Hz at the left end
Trims the pitch of the tone core by up to a semitone either way
Sets how far the pitch is modulated: by the delay's feedback with TONIC MOD unpatched, or by the voltage there when it is patched
Morphs the core tone from a plain triangle through a subharmonic blend, even harmonics, wavefolding and a pulse to a bright folded tone
Scales the voltage at the TONES CV jack, -1 to +1, before it is added to the tone morph
Sets the delay time, 5ms fully left to 2.45 seconds fully right, on an exponential scale
Trims the delay time by up to 12% of the TIME knob's travel either way
Sets how far the delay time is modulated, up to about five semitones: by the subharmonic with TIME MOD unpatched, or by the voltage there when it is patched
Scales the voltage at the TIME CV jack, -1 to +1, before half of it is added to the delay time
Sets how long the delay's feedback persists, and with it how close the network runs to self-oscillation
Scales the voltage at the DECAY CV jack, -1 to +1, before it is added to the decay
Sets the cutoff of the lowpass in the feedback path, 18Hz fully left to 18.5kHz fully right, and how much of that filtered signal is passed at all
Scales the voltage at the FILTER CV jack, -1 to +1, before it is added to the filter setting
Sets how much of the delay tail is held and how brightly it ages; with ABSORB CV patched it turns into a unipolar attenuator on that voltage
Crossfades the result between the dry tone and the delay's output on an equal-power curve; with BLEND CV patched it turns into a unipolar attenuator on that voltage
Sets the level of the two result outputs, silent fully left
Sets the rate of the internal agitation gesture, one cycle a minute fully left to 1kHz fully right
Skews the agitation gesture between rise and fall, 8% of the cycle spent rising fully left and 92% fully right
Scales the voltage at the SPEED CV jack, 0 to 1, before it is added to the agitation rate
Held down it pushes the activation up, by up to 0.72 of its range according to the touch source
Held down it nudges the delay time, by up to 0.24 of the TIME knob's travel according to the touch source
Held down it opens the feedback filter, by up to 0.28 of the FILTER knob's travel according to the touch source
Held down it pulls Absorb down by up to 0.58, which crumbles the delay tail
Held down it bends the pitch, by the touch source, the delay's feedback and the agitation gesture together
Held down it pushes Decay up by up to 0.43, towards unstable persistence
Sets the size of the reverb tank, a close haze fully left and a wide space fully right
Sets how long the reverb tail lasts, its loop gain running from 0.52 fully left to 0.985 fully right
Sets the density of the diffusion at the reverb's input and inside its tank
Sets the damping brightness of the reverb, 850Hz fully left to 18kHz fully right
Sets the depth and rate of the slow modulation of the reverb's delay lines, 0.25ms at 0.035Hz fully left to 7.5ms at about 0.5Hz fully right
Crossfades the two result outputs between the dry result and the reverb, on an equal-power curve
External audio to be conditioned by STRENGTH, with ±5V taken as full scale; anything below 8Hz is removed
Gates the agitation: with nothing patched the gesture repeats on its own, and with a cable here it rises once while the voltage is above 1.5V and is held at zero below it
Shifts the agitation rate through SPEED AMT, 5V covering the whole of the SPEED knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Shifts the activation through ACT AMT, 5V covering the whole of the activation range
Modulates the pitch through TONIC AMT; patching it replaces the delay feedback that otherwise does the modulating
Shifts the tone morph through TONES AMT, 10V covering the whole of the TONES knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Adds to the pitch of the tone core at 1V per octave
Modulates the delay time through TIME MOD AMT; patching it replaces the subharmonic that otherwise does the modulating
Shifts the delay time through TIME CV AMT, 20V covering the whole of the TIME knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Adds to the delay time with no attenuator of its own, 10V covering the whole of the TIME knob's travel
Shifts the decay through DECAY AMT, 10V covering the whole of the DECAY knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Sets the dry-wet blend once it is patched, 5V for full wet, scaled by the BLEND knob acting as an attenuator
Shifts the filter through FILTER AMT, 10V covering the whole of the FILTER knob's travel; the total is held inside that travel
Sets Absorb once it is patched, 10V for the full amount, scaled by the ABSORB knob acting as an attenuator
The conditioned external signal at audio rate, ±10V
An envelope follower on the conditioned external signal, 0 to 10V
The level of the delay's feedback as a smoothed bipolar CV, ±5V
The internal agitation gesture, 0 to 6V
The plain triangle from the tone core at its tonic pitch, ±5V, taken before TONES
A square and triangle mixed together an octave below the tonic, ±5V
The result at modular level, ±5V, after LEVEL and the reverb blend
The result at line level, a little over ±1.5V, after LEVEL and the reverb blend
Note — LEVEL comes up fully left, so both result outputs are silent until it is raised
Note — the module makes sound with nothing patched: raise LEVEL and CONSTANT and the tone core plays on its own
Note — each of the six touch pads is momentary, and what it injects is set by the touch source on the panel menu, a manual plate by default
Note — the reverb's decay, tone and modulation are each nudged by how far the delay feedback is swinging, so they shift a little as CV2 does
Menu — Touch source: Manual plate, CV1, CV2, Agitation, Sub harmonics, Strength, Noise — chooses the signal the six touch pads inject while they are held
Menu — Strength calibration: Factory, Line gentle, Modular hot — sets the gain, drive ceiling and envelope times the external input's conditioning uses

lines: A 3HP random voltage source: a smoothly fluctuating random CV carrying jitter, slow interference and occasional voltage slips, with an attenuverting blend for a second signal
Shifts the output up or down, -5V fully left, none at centre and +5V fully right
Sets how often a new random target is chosen, one every 100 seconds fully left rising to six a second fully right
Sets the depth of the random voltage before OFFSET is added, none fully left and ±5V fully right
Crossfades the output from the internal random voltage towards the input jack, towards the input inverted when turned anticlockwise, and changes nothing while that jack is unpatched
A second signal for the B knob to crossfade to, with ±5V taken as full scale
The random voltage scaled by RANGE and shifted by OFFSET, clipped at ±10V and always one channel
Note — the output moves on its own with nothing patched at all; the input is there only for the crossfade
Note — two lamps show the sign of the output, green for positive and red for negative, and a yellow one shows the jitter and the voltage slips

Drift.notes: The B knob is read whatever is patched, but drift_core.vult line 133 sets the blend amount to zero unless the input jack is connected, so with nothing patched the knob has no effect on the output. The speed range is 0.01Hz to 6Hz: drift_core.vult line 33 raises e to 6.396929655 times the shaped knob, which is a factor of 600.
